plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay only that second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks winning at a price above value, while underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since this is a one-shot game with no repeated interaction to exploit, the safest and most profit-maximizing action is to bid exactly my private value of $20.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (paying that amount, guaranteeing profit), and you avoid overpaying when your value is lower. Since this is a one-shot game with no repeated learning needed, the optimal approach is straightforward truthful bidding at $28, my private value.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do. Since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding above my value risks paying more than the item is worth, and bidding below reduces my chance of winning a profitable auction. With a value of $8, the optimal bid is simply $8, ensuring I maximize expected profit given the strategic properties of second-price auctions.
